'''Gabriel Nnamdi Vincent''' (born June 14, 1996) is a Nigerian-American professional [[basketball]] player who last played for the [[Atlanta Hawks]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). He also represents the [[Nigeria men's national basketball team|Nigerian national basketball team]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Aminu, Obekpa, Okoye arrive as D'Tigers open FIBA World Cup camp|url=https://guardian.ng/sport/aminu-obekpa-okoye-arrive-as-dtigers-open-fiba-world-cup-camp/|location=Lagos, Nigeria|date=July 11, 2018|access-date=August 27, 2019|newspaper=[[The Guardian (Nigeria)|The Guardian]]}}</ref> He played [[college basketball]] for the [[UC Santa Barbara Gauchos men's basketball|UC Santa Barbara Gauchos]]. Undrafted out of college, Vincent signed with the [[Stockton Kings]] of the [[NBA G League]] before joining the [[Miami Heat]] on a [[two-way contract]]. With Miami, he reached the [[NBA Finals]] in [[2020 NBA Finals|2020]] and [[2023 NBA Finals|2023]] before signing with the [[Los Angeles Lakers]].

==Early life and education==
Vincent was born in [[Modesto, California]], to Franklyn and Cynthia Vincent.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Gabe Vincent – 2017–18 – Men's Basketball |url=https://ucsbgauchos.com/sports/mens-basketball/roster/gabe-vincent/548 |access-date=2023-12-04 |website=University of California, Santa Barbara |language=en}}</ref> His father is [[Nigeria]]n and his American mother is from [[Connecticut]]. They both earned [[doctorate]]s in [[psychology]].<ref name=ca_02112021>{{cite news|title=During Our Interview It Is Clear To See That Vincent Has An Intense Work Ethic, Is Very Grounded, Humble, And Is A Man of Strong Faith|date=February 11, 2021|work=Contemporary Approaches|url=https://www.contemporaryapproaches.com/gabe-vincent-|access-date=July 11, 2021}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|first=Joe|last=Beguiristain|title=HEAT Proud Of Their Connection To Nigeria|date=May 25, 2021|website=Heat.com|url=https://www.nba.com/heat/news/heat-nigeria-connection-210525|access-date=July 11, 2021}}</ref> The youngest of three brothers, Vincent attended [[St. Mary's High School (Stockton, California)|St. Mary's High School]] in [[Stockton, California|Stockton]].<ref name=ca_02112021/>

Vincent played college basketball for [[UC Santa Barbara Gauchos men's basketball|University of California, Santa Barbara]] from 2014 to 2018, averaging 12.8 points in 113 games. After his senior season, he was named to the 2018 All-[[Big West]] Second Team.

==Career==
=== Sacramento Kings (2018–2020)===
After graduating, Vincent had a pre-draft workout with the [[Sacramento Kings]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Stockton product Gabe Vincent participates in Kings pre-draft workout |url=https://www.abc10.com/video/sports/nba/sacramento-kings/stockton-product-gabe-vincent-participates-in-kings-pre-draft-workout/103-8135897 |access-date=August 27, 2019 |work=[[KXTV]] |date=May 21, 2018}}</ref> Although he went undrafted in the [[2018 NBA draft]], he signed an Exhibit 10 contract with Sacramento on October 2.<ref>{{cite news |last=Klan |first=Mike |date=October 3, 2018 |title=Former Gaucho Gabe Vincent signs contract with Sacramento Kings |work=[[KEYT-TV]] |url=https://www.keyt.com/sports/former-gaucho-gabe-vincent-signs-contract-with-sacramento-kings/802787946 |access-date=August 27, 2019 |archive-date=March 8, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190308002957/https://www.keyt.com/sports/former-gaucho-gabe-vincent-signs-contract-with-sacramento-kings/802787946 |url-status=dead }}</ref> He was waived a few days later.<ref>{{cite news |last=Ham |first=James |date=October 13, 2018 |title=Breaking down Kings' roster ahead of NBA's mandatory cut down day |work=[[NBC Sports]] |url=https://www.nbcsports.com/bayarea/kings/breaking-down-kings-roster-ahead-nbas-mandatory-cut-down-day |access-date=August 27, 2019}}</ref>
He played 24 games, with three starts, for the [[Stockton Kings]] of the [[NBA G League]] during the [[2018–19 NBA G League season|2018–19 season]], averaging 8.8 points in 18.6 minutes per game.<ref>{{cite news |last=Schmidt |first=Dakota |date=August 25, 2019 |title=Look at Five Players With G League Experience To Keep An Eye On During The FIBA World Cup |work=[[SB Nation]] |url=https://www.ridiculousupside.com/2019/8/25/20831202/nba-gleague-fiba-world-cup-derrick-white-gabe-vincent-bruno-caboclo-brady-heslip-yuta-watanabe |access-date=August 27, 2019}}</ref> He scored 35 points in a game twice for the Kings in December 2019.<ref>{{cite news |date=December 21, 2019 |title=Local Roundup: Gabe Vincent scores 35 points again for G-Kings |work=The Record |url=https://www.recordnet.com/sports/20191221/local-roundup-gabe-vincent-scores-35-points-again-for-g-kings |url-status=dead |access-date=January 7, 2020 |archive-date=December 23, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191223190748/https://www.recordnet.com/sports/20191221/local-roundup-gabe-vincent-scores-35-points-again-for-g-kings }}</ref> Vincent played in 20 games (three starts) in his second season with Stockton while averaging 23.4 points, 3.8 rebounds, 2.5 assists and 1.30 steals per game and shooting 46.9 percent from the field, 41.2 percent from three-point range and 89.7 percent from the free throw line.<ref name=heat/>

===Miami Heat (2020–2023)===
On January 8, 2020, the [[Miami Heat]] announced that they had signed Vincent to a [[two-way contract]].<ref name=heat>{{cite web|title=GABE VINCENT GETS TWO-WAY OPPORTUNITY WITH HEAT|url=https://www.nba.com/heat/news/heat-sign-gabe-vincent-to-two-way-contract|website=NBA.com|access-date=January 8, 2020|date=January 8, 2020}}</ref> He made his NBA debut against the [[Orlando Magic]] on January 29.<ref>{{cite news |last=Taheri |first=Hannah |title=Stockton Native, Kings Alum Gabe Vincent Earns First NBA Action |url=https://stockton.gleague.nba.com/news/stockton-native-kings-alum-gabe-vincent-earns-first-nba-action/ |access-date=June 13, 2020 |work=NBA.com |date=January 29, 2020 |archive-date=January 12, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210112111801/https://stockton.gleague.nba.com/news/stockton-native-kings-alum-gabe-vincent-earns-first-nba-action/ |url-status=dead }}</ref> In the G League, Vincent tallied 27 points, three assists and one rebound in a win over the [[Salt Lake City Stars]] on February 3.<ref>{{cite news |title=Heat's Gabe Vincent: Superb offensive outing |url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/heats-gabe-vincent-superb-offensive-outing/ |access-date=June 13, 2020 |work=[[CBS Sports]] |date=February 4, 2020}}</ref> He averaged 20.9 points, 3.1 rebounds and 2.3 assists per game in 31 G League games. On June 22, 2020, the NBA G League announced that Vincent won the [[NBA G League Most Improved Player Award|Most Improved Player]] award.<ref>{{cite news |last=Beguiristain |first=Joe |date=June 22, 2020 |title=Sioux Falls Skyforce's Gabe Vincent Named 2019–20 NBA G League Most Improved Player |work=nba.com |url=https://www.nba.com/heat/news/gabe-vincent-named-nba-g-league-most-improved-player2020 |access-date=April 10, 2023}}</ref> The Heat reached the [[2020 NBA Finals]], but lost in six games to the [[Los Angeles Lakers]].

On August 1, 2021, Vincent joined the Heat for the [[NBA Summer League]]<ref>{{cite web|title=2021 Miami HEAT Summer League Roster|url=https://www.nba.com/heat/news/heat-announce-summer-league-roster-2021|website=NBA.com|date=August 1, 2021|access-date=September 11, 2021}}</ref> and five days later, he signed a standard contract with the Heat.<ref>{{cite web |last=Herrera |first=Irene |date=August 6, 2021 |title=HEAT RE-SIGNS GABE VINCENT |url=https://www.nba.com/heat/news/heat-resign-gabe-vincent |access-date=April 10, 2023 |website=NBA.com}}</ref>

In game 3 of the [[2023 NBA playoffs|2023 Eastern Conference Finals]], Vincent scored a playoff career high of 29 points in a 128–102 win to give the Heat a 3–0 lead over the [[Boston Celtics]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Heat roll past Celtics 128–102, take 3–0 lead in Eastern Conference finals|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap/_/gameId/401547673|website=ESPN.com|date=May 21, 2023|access-date=June 13, 2023}}</ref> The Heat eventually advanced to the NBA Finals after winning the series in seven games. In game 2 of the [[2023 NBA Finals]], Vincent had a team-high 23 points in a 111–108 win over the [[Denver Nuggets]] to tie the series 1–1.<ref>{{Cite web |date=June 4, 2023 |title=The Miami Heat roar back in Game 2 to tie the Denver Nuggets in NBA Finals |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap/_/gameId/401544847 |access-date=June 13, 2023 |website=ESPN.com|agency=Associated Press}}</ref> Vincent struggled to shoot from the three-point line in the NBA Finals, shooting just 33% from beyond the arc.{{citation needed|date=July 2023}} The Heat went on to lose the series in five games.

===Los Angeles Lakers (2023–2026)===
On July 6, 2023, Vincent signed a three-year, $33 million contract with the [[Los Angeles Lakers]].<ref>{{cite web |date=July 6, 2023 |title=Los Angeles Lakers Sign Gabe Vincent |url=https://www.nba.com/lakers/news/los-angeles-lakers-sign-gabe-vincent-070623 |access-date=October 17, 2024 |work=NBA.com}}</ref> He made only 11 appearances for the Lakers in the [[2023–24 NBA season]], averaging 3.1 points, 0.8 rebounds and 1.9 assists.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Gabe Vincent 2023–24 Stats per Game|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/player/gamelog/_/id/3137259/type/nba/year/2024|access-date=February 11, 2026|website=espn.com|language=en}}</ref>

Vincent made 72 appearances (including 11 starts) for Los Angeles during the [[2024–25 NBA season|2024–25 season]], averaging 6.4 points, 1.3 rebounds and 1.4 assists.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Gabe Vincent 2024–25 Stats per Game|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/player/gamelog/_/id/3137259/type/nba/year/2025|access-date=February 11, 2026|website=espn.com|language=en}}</ref> He played in 29 games (including seven starts) for the team in the [[2025–26 NBA season|2025–26 season]], posting averages of 4.8 points, 0.9 rebounds and 1.3 assists.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Gabe Vincent 2025–26 Stats per Game|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/player/gamelog/_/id/3137259/type/nba/year/2026|access-date=February 11, 2026|website=espn.com|language=en}}</ref>

===Atlanta Hawks (2026)===
On February 5, 2026, Vincent and a future second-round pick were traded to the [[Atlanta Hawks]] in exchange for guard [[Luke Kennard]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2026-02-05 |title=Atlanta Hawks Acquire Guard Gabe Vincent and Second-Round Draft Pick from Los Angeles Lakers |url=https://hawks.com/news/atlanta-hawks-acquire-guard-gabe-vincent-and-second-round-draft-pick-from-los-angeles-lakers |access-date=2026-02-25 |website=hawks.com |language=en}}</ref>

===National team career===
Vincent represents the [[Nigeria men's national basketball team|Nigerian national team]], D'Tigers. On August 24, 2019, he scored 23 points against [[Poland men's national basketball team|Poland]], including the game-winning three-pointer with 0.3 seconds left.<ref>{{cite news |title=Nigeria defeats Poland in "Peak International Tournament" |url=https://www.eurohoops.net/en/fibawc/923221/nigeria-defeats-poland-in-peak-international-tournament/ |access-date=August 27, 2019 |work=eurohoops.net |date=August 24, 2019}}</ref>
He represented the Nigerian team at the [[2019 FIBA Basketball World Cup]] in China.<ref>{{cite news |title=Nwora Releases D'tigers Final Roster For FIBA World Cup |url=https://www.channelstv.com/2019/08/27/nwora-releases-dtigers-final-roster-for-fiba-world-cup/ |access-date=August 27, 2019 |work=[[Channels TV]] |date=August 27, 2019}}</ref>
